evidence.text: Primarily, $Na^{+}-O$ (DOL) has a lower binding energy compared to $Na^{+}-O$ (G2), as shown in Figure 2a. Additionally, $Na^{+}$ can form a stable five-membered chelation structure with the negative-charged multidentate oxygen of G2 molecules. This endows the G2-based electrolyte high ionic conductivity, but regretfully, impedes $Na^{+}$ desolvation. DOL is a low polarity and low melting point ( $-95\ ^{\circ}C$ ) cyclic ether that exhibits dipole-dipole interactions with G2. Explicitly, ${}^{1}H$ and ${}^{17}O$ nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) were studied in Figure 2b; Figure S1 (Supporting Information). ${}^{1}H$ (G2) displays an upfield chemical shift in G2/DOL than G2, while the chemical shift of the ${}^{17}O$ (G2) shifts downfield. This implies that the dipole-dipole interactions between G2 and DOL weaken the shielding effect of electron clouds of O (G2) on atomic nucleus, indicating a decrease in the electron cloud density of O (G2). This demonstrates that DOL attenuates the electronegativity of donor O (G2), thereby diminishing the coordination of G2. $^{[16]}$ Consequently, DOL was blended into 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2 with a volume ratio of 3:1 to prepare 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2/DOL for the low-temperature adaptive electrolyte. 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2 as the reference electrolyte was compared and analyzed.

evidence.text: We also have tested the low-temperature performance of 0.5 M NaPF $_{6}$ G2/DOL in the cathode material of SIBs. Na $_{3}$ V $_{2}$ (PO $_{4}$ ) $_{3}$ was selected as the cathode with Na metal anode to assemble a coin cell. Rate performance of Na||NVP coupled with both electrolytes were evaluated. NVP paired with 0.5 M NaPF $_{6}$ G2/DOL achieves a capacity of up to 74.7 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 10 C, while it exclusively remains 60.6 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 10 C with 0.5 M NaPF $_{6}$ G2, as demonstrated in Figures S22–S24 (Supporting Information). Surprisingly, it can operate normally at LT, and specifically preserve a capacity of 79.8 mAh g $^{-1}$ at $-40$ °C, which is equivalent to 80.0% of the capacity at 25 °C in Figure S25 (Supporting Information). This indicates that temperature-adaptive electrolytes are not only compatible with NVP, but can also upgrade the rate performance and low-temperature performance of NVP cathode. To further verify the feasibility of electrolytes in SIBs, the coin full cell with NVP cathode and pre-cycled HC anode was assembled and subjected to rate performance testing at 25 °C. It displays that the full cell coupled with 0.5 M NaPF $_{6}$ G2/DOL can still retain a capacity of 71.6 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 10 C, while the cell using 0.5 M NaPF $_{6}$ G2 can only bestow a capacity of 52.3 mAh g $^{-1}$ in Figure 6a.

evidence.text: Additionally, the performance of the full cell was evaluated at -40 °C and it was manifested that the full cell using 0.5 M NaPF $_{6}$ G2/DOL can preserve 64.8% of its capacity at 25 °C in Figure 6b. After 50 cycles of 0.1 C (10 mA g $^{-1}$ ) at 25 °C, the capacity retention rate was 95.7%, and then after 50 cycles of 0.1 C at -40 °C, the capacity retention rate was 92.8%, as shown in Figure 6c. To test the practical application of electrolytes, a piece pouch cell (45 mAh) was assembled for cycling testing in Figure 6d and Figure S26 (Supporting Information). After cycling 100 cycles at 25 °C, the capacity retention rate was 86.7%. Then, the pouch cell was cycled 100 cycles at -30 °C, and the capacity retention rate was 92.43% in Figure 6e. Therefore, 0.5 M NaPF $_{6}$ G2/DOL electrolyte with a temperature-adaptive solvent structure holds great potential in the practical application of SIBs. Additionally, the temperature-adapted solvation structure may widespreadly exist in G2/DOL derivative electrolytes. We have tested the low-temperature performance of G2/THF, DME/DOL and DME/THF based electrolytes, as shown in Figure S27 (Supporting Information). HC can still retain 242.5 mAh g $^{-1}$ , 243.9 mAh g $^{-1}$ and 247.7 mAh g $^{-1}$ in G2/THF, DME/DOL and DME/THF based electrolytes at -40 °C, with capacity retention rates of 95.71%, 95.41% and 95.44% after 200 cycles, respectively.

evidence.text: Typically, this is on account of faster ion diffusion of 0.5 M NaPF $_{6}$ G2/DOL paired with HC, resulting in smaller voltage polarization at high current densities and low temperatures. This allows HC to achieve higher capacity at low temperatures and high rates. Additionally, the cycling performance of the HC anode at 25, -40, and $-50^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ was tested in Figure 5j and Figures S20, and S21 (Supporting Information). Compared with $78.9\%$ of $0.5\mathrm{MNaPF}_6$ G2, the capacity retention rate of HC after 1000 cycles at $5\mathrm{C}$ in $0.5\mathrm{MNaPF}_6$ G2/DOL is as high as $88.5\%$ at $25^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , indicating that HC has better stability with high current densities in $0.5\mathrm{MNaPF}_6$ G2/DOL. Besides, HC exhibits excellent low-temperature performance in $0.5\mathrm{MNaPF}_6$ G2/DOL. After 900 cycles at $-40^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , the capacity retention rate is $91.9\%$ . The capacity retention rates after 200 cycles at $1\mathrm{C}$ at $25^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and $-50^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ are $94.48\%$ and $97.25\%$ , respectively. This superior performance is attributed to the low-temperature adaptive solvation structure. Enhanced anion coordination and weakened solvent coordination facilitate to the desolvation of $\mathrm{Na^{+}}$ on the HC and the formation of rich-inorganic SEI, resulting in more desirable than the currently reported low-temperature electrolytes for SIBs, as listed in Table S7 (Supporting Information).

evidence.text: In summary, we present a low-temperature adaptive electrolyte that is compatible with high $Na^{+}$ desolvation rates for SIBs by regulating solvation structure. Due to the weakened ion-dipole interaction of $Na^{+}-O$ (G2), 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2/DOL has a low-temperature responsive solvation structure. As the temperature decreases, solvent coordination reduces and anion coordination increases in the first solvated shell of $Na^{+}$ . The temperature-sensitive solvation structure accelerates the desolvation of $Na^{+}$ , mitigating the voltage polarization on the HC surface. This enables HC to achieve higher capacity retention at high current density and low temperatures, thereby enhancing the low-temperature performance of SIBs. The HC anode realized a high capacity of 220.8 mAh g $^{-1}$ (1 C) at -40 °C, with 91.9% capacity retention after 900 cycles. At -30 °C, the capacity retention rate of HC||NVP pouch cell after 100 cycles at 0.1 C is 92.43%, indicating that electrolytes with low-temperature adaptation can effectively improve the low-temperature performance of SIBs. Noteworthy, temperature-adapted solvation structures universally exist in G2/DOL derivative electrolytes, which have exceedingly outstanding low-temperature performance. This provides a new way for designing low-temperature sodium-ion batteries and broadens their application for energy storage in extremely cold regions.

evidence.text:
Yuewei Cui, Youxuan Ni, Yuankun Wang, Linyue Wang, Wenxuan Yang, Shuang Wu, Weiwei Xie, Kai Zhang, Zhenhua Yan,\* and Jun Chen\*

Sodium-ion batteries are applied to cold-resistant energy storage hindered by phase transitions and sluggish $Na^{+}$ migration of traditional carbonate-based electrolytes at low temperatures. The desolvation of $Na^{+}$ is a crucial step in impeding the transport of $Na^{+}$ , which primarily attributes to the robust solvent coordination of $Na^{+}$ . Herein, a low-temperature adaptive electrolyte with an ultraweakly coordinated 1,3-dioxolane (DOL) is designed for constructing anion-rich solvation structure in a diglyme (G2)-based electrolyte. The electronegativity of the oxygen atoms of G2 is attenuated by dipole-dipole interaction between DOL and G2. As the temperature drops, the weakened $Na^{+}-O$ (G2) interaction leads to increased anionic coordination and less solvent coordination, facilitating the desolvation of $Na^{+}$ . This anionic-enhanced solvation structure contributes to the formation of stable solid electrolyte interface at the hard carbon (HC) anode, which accelerates $Na^{+}$ transport and diminishing the voltage polarization at low temperatures. Consequently, the HC anode can retain a high capacity of 203.9 mAh g $^{-1}$ (1 C) at -50 °C, and the pouch cell composed of $HC||Na_{3}V_{2}(PO_{4})_{3}$ at -30 °C achieves a capacity retention of 92.43% after 100 cycles at 0.1 C.

evidence.text: Variable temperature viscosity tests were conducted on these two electrolytes in Figure 2i. Unlike the viscosity of 0.5 M NaPF $_{6}$ G2, which rises dramatically with decreasing temperatures, the viscosity of 0.5 M NaPF $_{6}$ G2/DOL bestows a slightly growth trend. Simultaneously, the ionic conductivity (IC) of the electrolytes was calculated based on the electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) measurements at different temperatures, as shown in Figure 2j. Preparation of Electrodes: To prepare the anodes, commercial $\mu$ -Sn powders ( $\geq99.5\%$ , 325 mesh, Alab Chem. Tech.), polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF, Dodochem), and acetylene black (AB, Dodochem) were uniformly mixed in a steel jar with a mass ratio of $\mu$ -Sn: AB: PVDF at 7:2:1. A suitable amount of N-methyl-2-pyrrolidone (NMP, 99.0%, Aladdin) was added dropwise into the jar to create a sticky slurry, which was then ball milled at 300 rpm for 4 h. The obtained slurry was evenly coated onto copper foil using a doctor blade and was dried overnight in a vacuum oven at 60 °C. The dried copper foil was punched into circular discs with a diameter of 10 mm, and the mass loading of $\mu$ -Sn was $\approx1.0-1.4$ mg cm $^{-2}$ . evidence.text: First of all, different ratios of THF and MTHF in the electrolyte are tested at -40 °C. As illustrated in Figure S3 (Supporting Information), the half cells using the electrolyte with a volume ratio of THF/MTHF (TMT) at 3:7 v v $^{-1}$ show the highest reversible capacity, surpassing the performance of THF, MTHF, and THF/MTHF at other ratios. Thus, the following discussion focuses on this electrolyte, denoted as N/TMT. Meanwhile, the other two electrolytes, NaPF $_{6}$ dissolved in THF (N/THF) or MTHF (N/MTHF), were used as references. Then, MD simulations are employed to unveil the solvation structures in N/THF, N/TMT, and N/MTHF at $-40\ ^{\circ}C$ . As shown in Figure 1a–c, all three electrolytes contain abundant CIP (contact-ion pair) and AGG (Aggregates) structures, where anions are incorporated in the solvation sheath together with solvent molecules. This feature facilitates the formation of inorganic-rich SEI exhibiting superior mechanical properties. Therefore, these structures are highly desirable for high-stability anode materials. $^{[13]}$ The careful examination of these structures reveals that the coordination numbers (CNs) of $Na^{+}-F$ in N/THF, N/TMT, and N/MTHF increase from 2.44, 2.92 to 3.08 (Figure 1d–f), attributing to the low dielectric constant and weak binding ability of MTHF. While those of $Na^{+}-O$ in N/THF, N/TMT, and N/MTHF decrease from 3.67, 2.59 to 2.24 as a consequence of the increasing anions in the solvation sheath.

evidence.text: The weak dipole-dipole interaction and reduced net charge of the solvation structures facilitate the charge transportation, especially $Na^{+}$ ions. Figure 2g compares the ionic conductivities of different electrolytes at -40 °C. N/TMT as the electrolyte shows the highest ionic conductivity (1.38 mS cm $^{-1}$ ). While the ionic conductivities of N/THF and N/MTHF are 0.31 and 0.25 mS cm $^{-1}$ respectively. The advantage of N/TMT in charge transfer also exhibited in the Na $^{+}$ transference number (t $_{Na+}$ ). As illustrated by Figure 2h, the electrolyte using TMT as the solvent results in a t $_{Na+}$ of 0.55 at -40 °C, much larger than those of N/THF (0.23) and N/MTHF (0.26). In this context, the Na-ion conductivity in the electrolyte is improved from 0.07 mS cm $^{-1}$ in N/THF and 0.06 mS cm $^{-1}$ in N/MTHF to 0.76 mS cm $^{-1}$ in N/TMT. Therefore, the Na-ion transfer is significantly promoted in TMT. This conclusion is also supported by the calculated diffusion coefficients. The mean-square displacement (MSD) of Na $^{+}$ indicates that N/TMT exhibits the largest Na-ion diffusion coefficient at -40 °C, surpassing those of N/THF and N/MTHF (Figure 2i). The changes in the solvation structures must change the electrolyte thermodynamics.

evidence.text: Furthermore, the fluorination strategy relies on the controlled decomposition of fluorinated solvents or fluorine-rich additives to form a NaF-enriched inorganic interface, which significantly improves interfacial stability. $^{[24-26]}$ However, low-polarity solvents (e.g., cyclic ethers) used in weakly solvating strategies suffer from insufficient dissociation of sodium salts, resulting in limited ionic conductivity and flammability concerns due to their low flash points. Concentrated electrolytes and fluorination systems are also associated with high-cost concerns. Therefore, addressing the coupled challenges of temperature-resistant bulk/interface stability, cost-effectiveness, and safety remains a significant obstacle for large-scale energy storage applications. Herein, we design a flame-retardant hybrid electrolyte by combining fire-retardant triethyl phosphate (TEP) and low-freezing-point and weak-coordination methyl propionate (MP) solvents, which may offer the advantages of an anion-reinforced weak solvation structure, high nonflammability, and enhanced ionic conductivity at medium concentration (2 M). Fire-retardant TEP serves as the primary solvent to ensure salt solubility and nonflammability, while the introduction of MP, characterized by a lower freezing points and low dipole moment, aims to enhance ionic conductivity, reduce solvation energy, and facilitate the incorporation of additional anions into the Na $^{+}$ solvation structure.

evidence.text: The Na+-MP complex exhibits a low binding energy (-1.38 eV), consistent with its low DN value, further validating the weak coordination ability of MP. The redox behavior of the electrolyte was further evaluated using molecular orbital theory (Figure S3, Supporting Information). PF6− possesses the lowest highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) energy level (-10.16 eV), indicating strong resistance to electron loss and enhanced oxidative stability. Moreover, its low lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO) suggests preferential decomposition at the negative electrode, thereby improving interfacial compatibility with TEP. Based on optimizations in nonflammability, ionic conductivity and long cycle performance, the 2.0 M NaPF6 in TEP/MP +1 wt% VC (6:4 by volume ratio, denoted as NTM) is selected as the optimal electrolyte for further investigation (Figures S2 and S4, Supporting Information), with 2.0 M NaPF6 dissolved in TEP +1 wt% VC (denoted as NT) and traditional carbonate electrolyte 1.0 M NaPF6 in PC (denoted as NP) serving as control groups. Moreover, the NTM electrolyte not only exhibits a reduced contact angle with the separator (Figure S5, Supporting Information), indicative of decreased electrolyte viscosity and improved wettability, but also shows an oxidation potential of up to 4.52 V and a lower reduction potential (Figure S6, Supporting Information).

evidence.text: Furthermore, the NTM electrolyte enables excellent rate performance at 50 °C and even stable cycling at an extreme temperature of 80 °C (Figures S25 and S26, Supporting Information). This superior performance is attributed to the formation of a robust NaF-enriched interface and thermally stable TEP. At -40 °C, the NVP||Na cell with NP electrolyte delivers only 22.8 mA h g $^{-1}$ after 100 cycles at 50 mA g $^{-1}$ , owing to its low ionic conductivity and sluggish ion transport. The NT-based cell fails rapidly due to partial electrolyte solidification and high ion transfer activation energy (Figure 4b). Conversely, the NVP||Na cell with NTM electrolyte delivers 64.8 mA h g $^{-1}$ and 95.6% capacity retention after 100 cycles (Figure 4d,e; Figure S27, Supporting Information), underscoring its superior competitiveness (Table S4, Supporting Information). The NTM electrolyte also exhibits high specific capacities at various current rates even under the extremely low temperature of -40 °C, delivering 80.0, 72.3, 62.7, and 51.6 mA h g $^{-1}$ at 10, 20, 50, and 100 mA g $^{-1}$ , respectively (Figure S28, Supporting Information).

evidence.text: To further validate the practicality of the NTM electrolyte, full cells with NVP cathodes and hard carbon (HC) anodes were constructed, operating within the voltage range of 2.0–3.6 V (Figure 5a). The NVP||HC full cell, without any presodiation treatment, exhibits a high specific capacity of 88.0 mA h g $^{-1}$ and excellent cycling stability over 100 cycles at 50 mA g $^{-1}$ , maintaining an impressive capacity retention of 84.9% in the NTM electrolyte. This retention markedly surpasses that of the conventional NP electrolyte (51.9%), as illustrated in Figure 5b,c. Furthermore, the full cell utilizing the NTM electrolyte demonstrates superior rate capability, delivering reversible capacities of 87.2, 82.0, 79.1, 77.0, 71.9, and 68.1 mA h g $^{-1}$ at 20, 50, 80, 100, 200, and 300 mA g $^{-1}$ , respectively (Figure 5d). The charge–discharge curves exhibit minimal polarization even at elevated rates (Figure S32, Supporting Information). In addition, the overall electrical performance of the NTM electrolyte is better than that of the NED (NP-EC/DMC) electrolyte (Figure S33, Supporting Information). Notably, the NVP||HC full cell with the NTM electrolyte maintains stable cycling for 500 cycles at a high current of 200 mA g $^{-1}$ (Figure S34, Supporting Information). Self-discharge behavior was further evaluated in the NVP||HC full-cell system. The results display that the NP electrolyte system retains 72.8% of its discharge capacity after 48 h of rest (based on 4th cycle).

claim_verdicts.quote: The half cells are based on CR2025 coins cells using the discs as the working electrode
claim_verdicts.basis: 该文献的电池形式为 CR2025 扣式电池，未见 45 mAh 级 HC||NVP 软包电池的循环数据。

claim_verdicts.chunk_id: 0004_Chang 等 - 2025 - Solvent-Fluorine-Free Anion-Enriched and Non-Flammable Electrolyte Enables Safe Sodium-Ion Battery::sec6::child3

claim_verdicts.basis: 该文献只给出扣式全电池与 NVP||Na 电池数据，未见 45 mAh 级软包电池的循环测试与保持率。

evidence_chunks.chunk_id: 0009_Cui 等 - 2025 - A Temperature-Adapted Ultraweakly Solvating Electrolyte for Cold-Resistant Sodium-Ion Batteries::sec2::child0
evidence_chunks.content: Primarily, $Na^{+}-O$ (DOL) has a lower binding energy compared to $Na^{+}-O$ (G2), as shown in Figure 2a. Additionally, $Na^{+}$ can form a stable five-membered chelation structure with the negative-charged multidentate oxygen of G2 molecules. This endows the G2-based electrolyte high ionic conductivity, but regretfully, impedes $Na^{+}$ desolvation. DOL is a low polarity and low melting point ( $-95\ ^{\circ}C$ ) cyclic ether that exhibits dipole-dipole interactions with G2. Explicitly, ${}^{1}H$ and ${}^{17}O$ nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) were studied in Figure 2b; Figure S1 (Supporting Information). ${}^{1}H$ (G2) displays an upfield chemical shift in G2/DOL than G2, while the chemical shift of the ${}^{17}O$ (G2) shifts downfield. This implies that the dipole-dipole interactions between G2 and DOL weaken the shielding effect of electron clouds of O (G2) on atomic nucleus, indicating a decrease in the electron cloud density of O (G2). This demonstrates that DOL attenuates the electronegativity of donor O (G2), thereby diminishing the coordination of G2. $^{[16]}$ Consequently, DOL was blended into 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2 with a volume ratio of 3:1 to prepare 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2/DOL for the low-temperature adaptive electrolyte. 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2 as the reference electrolyte was compared and analyzed.

evidence_chunks.chunk_id: 0009_Cui 等 - 2025 - A Temperature-Adapted Ultraweakly Solvating Electrolyte for Cold-Resistant Sodium-Ion Batteries::sec5::child0
evidence_chunks.content: We also have tested the low-temperature performance of 0.5 M NaPF $_{6}$ G2/DOL in the cathode material of SIBs. Na $_{3}$ V $_{2}$ (PO $_{4}$ ) $_{3}$ was selected as the cathode with Na metal anode to assemble a coin cell. Rate performance of Na||NVP coupled with both electrolytes were evaluated. NVP paired with 0.5 M NaPF $_{6}$ G2/DOL achieves a capacity of up to 74.7 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 10 C, while it exclusively remains 60.6 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 10 C with 0.5 M NaPF $_{6}$ G2, as demonstrated in Figures S22–S24 (Supporting Information). Surprisingly, it can operate normally at LT, and specifically preserve a capacity of 79.8 mAh g $^{-1}$ at $-40$ °C, which is equivalent to 80.0% of the capacity at 25 °C in Figure S25 (Supporting Information). This indicates that temperature-adaptive electrolytes are not only compatible with NVP, but can also upgrade the rate performance and low-temperature performance of NVP cathode. To further verify the feasibility of electrolytes in SIBs, the coin full cell with NVP cathode and pre-cycled HC anode was assembled and subjected to rate performance testing at 25 °C. It displays that the full cell coupled with 0.5 M NaPF $_{6}$ G2/DOL can still retain a capacity of 71.6 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 10 C, while the cell using 0.5 M NaPF $_{6}$ G2 can only bestow a capacity of 52.3 mAh g $^{-1}$ in Figure 6a.

evidence_chunks.chunk_id: 0009_Cui 等 - 2025 - A Temperature-Adapted Ultraweakly Solvating Electrolyte for Cold-Resistant Sodium-Ion Batteries::sec5::child1
evidence_chunks.content: Additionally, the performance of the full cell was evaluated at -40 °C and it was manifested that the full cell using 0.5 M NaPF $_{6}$ G2/DOL can preserve 64.8% of its capacity at 25 °C in Figure 6b. After 50 cycles of 0.1 C (10 mA g $^{-1}$ ) at 25 °C, the capacity retention rate was 95.7%, and then after 50 cycles of 0.1 C at -40 °C, the capacity retention rate was 92.8%, as shown in Figure 6c. Additionally, the temperature-adapted solvation structure may widespreadly exist in G2/DOL derivative electrolytes. We have tested the low-temperature performance of G2/THF, DME/DOL and DME/THF based electrolytes, as shown in Figure S27 (Supporting Information). HC can still retain 242.5 mAh g $^{-1}$ , 243.9 mAh g $^{-1}$ and 247.7 mAh g $^{-1}$ in G2/THF, DME/DOL and DME/THF based electrolytes at -40 °C, with capacity retention rates of 95.71%, 95.41% and 95.44% after 200 cycles, respectively.

## 配方筛选结果
已整理候选资料，当前暂缓推荐。未满足的条件列在下方。

### 候选资料：candidate-1（尚未获推荐）
以下为候选记录中的组成，配制时须核对所引原文的比例基准与用量。
盐：NaPF6；浓度：0.5 mol L⁻¹；NaPF6：0.5 mol L⁻¹；溶剂：G2 (diglyme), DOL (1,3-dioxolane)；溶剂比例（体积）：DOL (1,3-dioxolane)=1.0, G2 (diglyme)=3.0。
- 配方原文 [0009_Cui 等 - 2025 - A Temperature-Adapted Ultraweakly Solvating Electrolyte for Cold-Resistant Sodium-Ion Batteries::sec2::child0]：Primarily, $Na^{+}-O$ (DOL) has a lower binding energy compared to $Na^{+}-O$ (G2), as shown in Figure 2a. Additionally, $Na^{+}$ can form a stable five-membered chelation structure with the negative-charged multidentate oxygen of G2 molecules. This endows the G2-based electrolyte high ionic conductivity, but regretfully, impedes $Na^{+}$ desolvation. DOL is a low polarity and low melting point ( $-95\ ^{\circ}C$ ) cyclic ether that exhibits dipole-dipole interactions with G2. Explicitly, ${}^{1}H$ and ${}^{17}O$ nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) were studied in Figure 2b; Figure S1 (Supporting Information). ${}^{1}H$ (G2) displays an upfield chemical shift in G2/DOL than G2, while the chemical shift of the ${}^{17}O$ (G2) shifts downfield. This implies that the dipole-dipole interactions between G2 and DOL weaken the shielding effect of electron clouds of O (G2) on atomic nucleus, indicating a decrease in the electron cloud density of O (G2). This demonstrates that DOL attenuates the electronegativity of donor O (G2), thereby diminishing the coordination of G2. $^{[16]}$ Consequently, DOL was blended into 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2 with a volume ratio of 3:1 to prepare 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2/DOL for the low-temperature adaptive electrolyte. 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2 as the reference electrolyte was compared and analyzed.

### 候选资料：candidate-2（尚未获推荐）
以下为候选记录中的组成，配制时须核对所引原文的比例基准与用量。
盐：NaPF6；浓度：1 mol L⁻¹；NaPF6：1 mol L⁻¹；溶剂：THF (tetrahydrofuran), MTHF (2-methyltetrahydrofuran)；溶剂比例（体积）：MTHF (2-methyltetrahydrofuran)=7.0, THF (tetrahydrofuran)=3.0。
- 配方原文 [0047_Lv 等 - 2025 - Anion-Dipole Repulsions Improve Low-Temperature Performance of μ-Sn for Advanced Sodium-Ion Batterie::sec5::child0]：Materials: $NaPF_{6}$ was purchased from Dodochem. Tetrahydrofuran (THF), 2-methyltetrahydrofuran (MTHF), 3-methyltetrahydrofuran (3-MTHF), 1,3-dioxane (DOL), 2-methyl-1,3-dioxolane (2-MDOL), 4-methyl-1,3-dioxolane (4-MDOL), tetrahydropyran (THP), 1,3-dioxane (1,3-DX) and 1,4-dioxane (1,4-DX) were ordered from Aladdin. The electrolytes were obtained by dissolving 1 M $NaPF_{6}$ in THF/cyclic ethers with different volume ratios. All the electrolytes were kept overnight prior to use to ensure complete dissolution. Preparation of Electrodes: To prepare the anodes, commercial $\mu$ -Sn powders ( $\geq99.5\%$ , 325 mesh, Alab Chem. Tech.), polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF, Dodochem), and acetylene black (AB, Dodochem) were uniformly mixed in a steel jar with a mass ratio of $\mu$ -Sn: AB: PVDF at 7:2:1. A suitable amount of N-methyl-2-pyrrolidone (NMP, 99.0%, Aladdin) was added dropwise into the jar to create a sticky slurry, which was then ball milled at 300 rpm for 4 h. The obtained slurry was evenly coated onto copper foil using a doctor blade and was dried overnight in a vacuum oven at 60 °C. The dried copper foil was punched into circular discs with a diameter of 10 mm, and the mass loading of $\mu$ -Sn was $\approx1.0-1.4$ mg cm $^{-2}$ . To prepare the cathodes, Na $_{3}$ V $_{2}$ (PO $_{4}$ ) $_{3}$ @C (NVP@C) was synthesized by a reported method. NVP@C, AB, and PVDF were uniformly mixed with a weight ratio of 8:1:1.
- 配方原文 [0047_Lv 等 - 2025 - Anion-Dipole Repulsions Improve Low-Temperature Performance of μ-Sn for Advanced Sodium-Ion Batterie::sec3::child1]：First of all, different ratios of THF and MTHF in the electrolyte are tested at -40 °C. As illustrated in Figure S3 (Supporting Information), the half cells using the electrolyte with a volume ratio of THF/MTHF (TMT) at 3:7 v v $^{-1}$ show the highest reversible capacity, surpassing the performance of THF, MTHF, and THF/MTHF at other ratios. Thus, the following discussion focuses on this electrolyte, denoted as N/TMT. Meanwhile, the other two electrolytes, NaPF $_{6}$ dissolved in THF (N/THF) or MTHF (N/MTHF), were used as references. Then, MD simulations are employed to unveil the solvation structures in N/THF, N/TMT, and N/MTHF at $-40\ ^{\circ}C$ . As shown in Figure 1a–c, all three electrolytes contain abundant CIP (contact-ion pair) and AGG (Aggregates) structures, where anions are incorporated in the solvation sheath together with solvent molecules. This feature facilitates the formation of inorganic-rich SEI exhibiting superior mechanical properties. Therefore, these structures are highly desirable for high-stability anode materials. $^{[13]}$ The careful examination of these structures reveals that the coordination numbers (CNs) of $Na^{+}-F$ in N/THF, N/TMT, and N/MTHF increase from 2.44, 2.92 to 3.08 (Figure 1d–f), attributing to the low dielectric constant and weak binding ability of MTHF. While those of $Na^{+}-O$ in N/THF, N/TMT, and N/MTHF decrease from 3.67, 2.59 to 2.24 as a consequence of the increasing anions in the solvation sheath.

### 候选资料：candidate-3（尚未获推荐）
以下为候选记录中的组成，配制时须核对所引原文的比例基准与用量。
盐：NaPF6；浓度：2 mol L⁻¹；NaPF6：2 mol L⁻¹；溶剂：TEP (triethyl phosphate), MP (methyl propionate)；溶剂比例（体积）：MP (methyl propionate)=4.0, TEP (triethyl phosphate)=6.0。
- 配方原文 [0004_Chang 等 - 2025 - Solvent-Fluorine-Free Anion-Enriched and Non-Flammable Electrolyte Enables Safe Sodium-Ion Battery::sec1::child3]：Furthermore, the fluorination strategy relies on the controlled decomposition of fluorinated solvents or fluorine-rich additives to form a NaF-enriched inorganic interface, which significantly improves interfacial stability. $^{[24-26]}$ However, low-polarity solvents (e.g., cyclic ethers) used in weakly solvating strategies suffer from insufficient dissociation of sodium salts, resulting in limited ionic conductivity and flammability concerns due to their low flash points. Concentrated electrolytes and fluorination systems are also associated with high-cost concerns. Therefore, addressing the coupled challenges of temperature-resistant bulk/interface stability, cost-effectiveness, and safety remains a significant obstacle for large-scale energy storage applications. Herein, we design a flame-retardant hybrid electrolyte by combining fire-retardant triethyl phosphate (TEP) and low-freezing-point and weak-coordination methyl propionate (MP) solvents, which may offer the advantages of an anion-reinforced weak solvation structure, high nonflammability, and enhanced ionic conductivity at medium concentration (2 M). Fire-retardant TEP serves as the primary solvent to ensure salt solubility and nonflammability, while the introduction of MP, characterized by a lower freezing points and low dipole moment, aims to enhance ionic conductivity, reduce solvation energy, and facilitate the incorporation of additional anions into the Na $^{+}$ solvation structure.
- 配方原文 [0004_Chang 等 - 2025 - Solvent-Fluorine-Free Anion-Enriched and Non-Flammable Electrolyte Enables Safe Sodium-Ion Battery::sec2::child2]：The Na+-MP complex exhibits a low binding energy (-1.38 eV), consistent with its low DN value, further validating the weak coordination ability of MP. The redox behavior of the electrolyte was further evaluated using molecular orbital theory (Figure S3, Supporting Information). PF6− possesses the lowest highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) energy level (-10.16 eV), indicating strong resistance to electron loss and enhanced oxidative stability. Moreover, its low lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO) suggests preferential decomposition at the negative electrode, thereby improving interfacial compatibility with TEP. Based on optimizations in nonflammability, ionic conductivity and long cycle performance, the 2.0 M NaPF6 in TEP/MP +1 wt% VC (6:4 by volume ratio, denoted as NTM) is selected as the optimal electrolyte for further investigation (Figures S2 and S4, Supporting Information), with 2.0 M NaPF6 dissolved in TEP +1 wt% VC (denoted as NT) and traditional carbonate electrolyte 1.0 M NaPF6 in PC (denoted as NP) serving as control groups. Moreover, the NTM electrolyte not only exhibits a reduced contact angle with the separator (Figure S5, Supporting Information), indicative of decreased electrolyte viscosity and improved wettability, but also shows an oxidation potential of up to 4.52 V and a lower reduction potential (Figure S6, Supporting Information).

## 候选评估
### candidate-1
评估建议：候选与文献配方身份一致，且在 -30 °C 45 mAh 软包 100 次循环（92.43%）与 -40 °C 扣式全电池 50 次循环（92.8%）均有良好保持率；但未见 -40 °C、45 mAh 软包、100 次循环的直接实测，也无原文对 -30 °C 结果向 -40 °C 软包的可转移说明，故暂不作出推荐，待补齐该确切条件证据后再定。
任务要求与已有依据（模型语义判断，程序核验出处）：
- Salt identity NaPF6 at 0.5 M concentration：原文明确以 0.5 M NaPF6 G2/DOL 作为低温自适应电解液并与 0.5 M NaPF6 G2 对照，盐与浓度与候选一致。 [0009_Cui 等 - 2025 - A Temperature-Adapted Ultraweakly Solvating Electrolyte for Cold-Resistant Sodium-Ion Batteries::sec2::child0]
- Solvent blend G2/DOL at 3:1 volume ratio：原文说明将 DOL 以 3:1 体积比混入 0.5 M NaPF6 G2 制得 0.5 M NaPF6 G2/DOL，与候选的 G2:DOL=3:1（体积）一致。 [0009_Cui 等 - 2025 - A Temperature-Adapted Ultraweakly Solvating Electrolyte for Cold-Resistant Sodium-Ion Batteries::sec2::child0]
- HC||NVP full-cell chemistry：原文以硬碳负极与 Na3V2(PO4)3 正极组装全电池并评价，组成与候选目标体系一致。 [0009_Cui 等 - 2025 - A Temperature-Adapted Ultraweakly Solvating Electrolyte for Cold-Resistant Sodium-Ion Batteries::sec6::child0]
- 45 mAh pouch cell format：原文为测试实际应用组装了 45 mAh 软包电池并进行循环测试。 [0009_Cui 等 - 2025 - A Temperature-Adapted Ultraweakly Solvating Electrolyte for Cold-Resistant Sodium-Ion Batteries::sec5::child1]
- Pouch cell operated at -40 °C for 100 cycles：45 mAh 软包的 100 次循环容量保持率是在 -30 °C 测得的（92.43%）；-40 °C 的循环数据来自扣式全电池（50 次，92.8%）与 HC 负极，并非软包 100 次循环，原文也未建立 -30 °C 结果可向 -40 °C 软包转移的关系。 [0009_Cui 等 - 2025 - A Temperature-Adapted Ultraweakly Solvating Electrolyte for Cold-Resistant Sodium-Ion Batteries::sec5::child1][0009_Cui 等 - 2025 - A Temperature-Adapted Ultraweakly Solvating Electrolyte for Cold-Resistant Sodium-Ion Batteries::sec5]
- Target observable is cycle-capacity retention：原文以容量保持率报告全电池与软包循环结果，与所需目标观测一致。 [0009_Cui 等 - 2025 - A Temperature-Adapted Ultraweakly Solvating Electrolyte for Cold-Resistant Sodium-Ion Batteries::sec5::child1]
文献与候选的关联：候选的盐、浓度与 G2/DOL=3:1 体积比与原文所制备的 0.5 M NaPF6 G2/DOL 完全对应；原文以该电解液组装 45 mAh HC||NVP 软包并在 -30 °C 循环 100 次给出 92.43% 保持率，同一电解液在 -40 °C 扣式全电池 50 次循环给出 92.8% 保持率，二者共同说明该配方在低温全电池中的循环表现，但未覆盖 -40 °C 软包 100 次这一确切条件。 [0009_Cui 等 - 2025 - A Temperature-Adapted Ultraweakly Solvating Electrolyte for Cold-Resistant Sodium-Ion Batteries::sec2::child0][0009_Cui 等 - 2025 - A Temperature-Adapted Ultraweakly Solvating Electrolyte for Cold-Resistant Sodium-Ion Batteries::sec5::child1]
### candidate-2
评估建议：The candidate is the literature's selected N/TMT electrolyte, demonstrated with HC||NVP@C full cells at -40 °C and 100-cycle HC cycling, directly supporting scientific applicability; the only unresolved item is scale-up to a 45 mAh pouch format, which is noted but does not overturn the electrolyte-level support.
任务要求与已有依据（模型语义判断，程序核验出处）：
- Sodium salt is NaPF6 at ~1 M concentration：The source prepares the low-temperature electrolyte by dissolving 1 M NaPF6 in THF/cyclic ether mixtures, matching the candidate's single NaPF6 salt at 1.0 M. [0047_Lv 等 - 2025 - Anion-Dipole Repulsions Improve Low-Temperature Performance of μ-Sn for Advanced Sodium-Ion Batterie::sec5::child0]
- Solvent system is THF/MTHF at 3:7 by volume：The paper states the THF/MTHF (TMT) mixed solvent at 3:7 v v^-1 gave the highest reversible capacity at -40 °C and was selected as N/TMT, matching the candidate's THF:MTHF = 3:7 volume ratio. [0047_Lv 等 - 2025 - Anion-Dipole Repulsions Improve Low-Temperature Performance of μ-Sn for Advanced Sodium-Ion Batterie::sec3::child1]
- Electrolyte is validated at -40 °C：N/TMT is repeatedly tested at -40 °C for half and full cells, confirming the operating temperature requirement. [0047_Lv 等 - 2025 - Anion-Dipole Repulsions Improve Low-Temperature Performance of μ-Sn for Advanced Sodium-Ion Batterie::sec3::child18]
- Cell chemistry is hard-carbon anode coupled with NVP cathode：The paper examines HC in half cells and explicitly reports HC||NVP@C full cells in N/TMT at -40 °C, matching the target HC||NVP chemistry. [0047_Lv 等 - 2025 - Anion-Dipole Repulsions Improve Low-Temperature Performance of μ-Sn for Advanced Sodium-Ion Batterie::sec3::child18][0047_Lv 等 - 2025 - Anion-Dipole Repulsions Improve Low-Temperature Performance of μ-Sn for Advanced Sodium-Ion Batterie::sec4::child2]
- Cycling for 100 cycles at -40 °C：The HC anode is reported to deliver 203.7 mAh g^-1 after 100 cycles at -40 °C in half cells using N/TMT, providing direct 100-cycle low-temperature evidence for this electrolyte and anode material. [0047_Lv 等 - 2025 - Anion-Dipole Repulsions Improve Low-Temperature Performance of μ-Sn for Advanced Sodium-Ion Batterie::sec3::child18]
- Target observable is cycle-capacity retention：The paper gives explicit capacity-retention values for the μ-Sn||NVP@C full cell (≈84.9%) but for the HC||NVP@C full cell only a capacity value (166.7 mAh g^-1) is reported without a stated retention; the retention observable for the HC target is therefore not directly quoted. [0047_Lv 等 - 2025 - Anion-Dipole Repulsions Improve Low-Temperature Performance of μ-Sn for Advanced Sodium-Ion Batterie::sec3::child18]
文献与候选的关联：The candidate is chemically identical to the paper's optimized N/TMT electrolyte (1 M NaPF6 in 3:7 v/v THF/MTHF), which is tested in CR2025 coin cells with glass-fiber separator and presodiated HC anode against NVP@C cathode at -40 °C. This establishes a direct electrolyte/anode/cathode/temperature association, but the cell format and nominal capacity differ from the target 45 mAh pouch cell, so the association supports the chemistry rather than the pouch-scale device. [0047_Lv 等 - 2025 - Anion-Dipole Repulsions Improve Low-Temperature Performance of μ-Sn for Advanced Sodium-Ion Batterie::sec5::child0][0047_Lv 等 - 2025 - Anion-Dipole Repulsions Improve Low-Temperature Performance of μ-Sn for Advanced Sodium-Ion Batterie::sec3::child18]
### candidate-3
评估建议：候选在盐（2.0 M NaPF6）、溶剂（TEP/MP 6:4 体积比）、HC||NVP 全电池构型与 -40 °C 可运行性上有原文支持，但目标可观测（-40 °C、100 次循环的全电池容量保持）在文献中仅见于 NVP||Na 半电池，全电池在 -40 °C 只报告 20 次循环；且 45 mAh 软包电芯身份未被确认，候选还缺少 NTM 配方中的 1 wt% VC。因此在当前证据下不给出推荐，暂持 hold。
任务要求与已有依据（模型语义判断，程序核验出处）：
- NaPF6 salt at 2.0 M concentration：原文明确以 2.0 M NaPF6 溶于 TEP/MP 作为 NTM 体系基础配方，与 candidate-3 的盐与浓度一致。 [0004_Chang 等 - 2025 - Solvent-Fluorine-Free Anion-Enriched and Non-Flammable Electrolyte Enables Safe Sodium-Ion Battery::sec2::child2]
- TEP/MP 溶剂体系以 6:4 体积比混合：原文给出 TEP/MP 6:4 by volume ratio 的 NTM 配方，与 candidate-3 的溶剂及体积比一致。 [0004_Chang 等 - 2025 - Solvent-Fluorine-Free Anion-Enriched and Non-Flammable Electrolyte Enables Safe Sodium-Ion Battery::sec2::child2]
- 用于 HC||NVP 全电池构型（硬碳负极 / NVP 正极）：原文明确构建了 NVP 正极与硬碳（HC）负极、2.0–3.6 V 的 NVP||HC 全电池，与目标构型一致。 [0004_Chang 等 - 2025 - Solvent-Fluorine-Free Anion-Enriched and Non-Flammable Electrolyte Enables Safe Sodium-Ion Battery::sec6::child0]
- 电解质在 -40 °C 下可运行（抗冻/低温工作能力）：原文 NVP||HC 全电池在 -40 °C 可成功运行并完成 20 次循环，且给出 -40 °C 放电容量，说明该体系在目标低温下可工作。 [0004_Chang 等 - 2025 - Solvent-Fluorine-Free Anion-Enriched and Non-Flammable Electrolyte Enables Safe Sodium-Ion Battery::sec6::child3]
- 在 -40 °C 下循环 100 次并报告容量保持率（目标可观测：循环容量保持）：原文在 -40 °C、100 次循环、95.6% 保持率的数据是在 NVP||Na 半电池上取得；而 NVP||HC 全电池在 -40 °C 仅报告 20 次循环（83.9% 保持），未给出全电池 -40 °C 100 次循环的保持率，也没有把半电池的 100 次循环结果明确转移到全电池，故目标循环条件在全电池上未被验证。 [0004_Chang 等 - 2025 - Solvent-Fluorine-Free Anion-Enriched and Non-Flammable Electrolyte Enables Safe Sodium-Ion Battery::sec5::child2][0004_Chang 等 - 2025 - Solvent-Fluorine-Free Anion-Enriched and Non-Flammable Electrolyte Enables Safe Sodium-Ion Battery::sec6::child3][0004_Chang 等 - 2025 - Solvent-Fluorine-Free Anion-Enriched and Non-Flammable Electrolyte Enables Safe Sodium-Ion Battery::sec1::child4]
- 目标电芯身份为 45 mAh 软包（pouch）电池：原文全电池数据以比容量（mA h g^-1，如 88.0 mA h g^-1）表述，属按活性物质质量归一量，并非电芯标称容量（mAh）；参考文献未报告 pouch 软包构型，也未报告 45 mAh 标称容量，故无法确认候选对应于 45 mAh 软包电芯身份。

- Primarily, $Na^{+}-O$ (DOL) has a lower binding energy compared to $Na^{+}-O$ (G2), as shown in Figure 2a. Additionally, $Na^{+}$ can form a stable five-membered chelation structure with the negative-charged multidentate oxygen of G2 molecules. This endows the G2-based electrolyte high ionic conductivity, but regretfully, impedes $Na^{+}$ desolvation. - We also have tested the low-temperature performance of 0.5 M NaPF $_{6}$ G2/DOL in the cathode material of SIBs. Na $_{3}$ V $_{2}$ (PO $_{4}$ ) $_{3}$ was selected as the cathode with Na metal anode to assemble a coin cell. Rate performance of Na||NVP coupled with both electrolytes were evaluated. - Additionally, the performance of the full cell was evaluated at -40 °C and it was manifested that the full cell using 0.5 M NaPF $_{6}$ G2/DOL can preserve 64.8% of its capacity at 25 °C in Figure 6b. source_refs.raw_quote: Primarily, $Na^{+}-O$ (DOL) has a lower binding energy compared to $Na^{+}-O$ (G2), as shown in Figure 2a. Additionally, $Na^{+}$ can form a stable five-membered chelation structure with the negative-charged multidentate oxygen of G2 molecules. This endows the G2-based electrolyte high ionic conductivity, but regretfully, impedes $Na^{+}$ desolvation. DOL is a low polarity and low melting point ( $-95\ ^{\circ}C$ ) cyclic ether that exhibits dipole-dipole interactions with G2. Explicitly, ${}^{1}H$ and ${}^{17}O$ nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) were studied in Figure 2b; Figure S1 (Supporting Information). ${}^{1}H$ (G2) displays an upfield chemical shift in G2/DOL than G2, while the chemical shift of the ${}^{17}O$ (G2) shifts downfield. This implies that the dipole-dipole interactions between G2 and DOL weaken the shielding effect of electron clouds of O (G2) on atomic nucleus, indicating a decrease in the electron cloud density of O (G2). This demonstrates that DOL attenuates the electronegativity of donor O (G2), thereby diminishing the coordination of G2. $^{[16]}$ Consequently, DOL was blended into 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2 with a volume ratio of 3:1 to prepare 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2/DOL for the low-temperature adaptive electrolyte. 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2 as the reference electrolyte was compared and analyzed.

Na $_{3}$ V $_{2}$ (PO $_{4}$ ) $_{3}$ was selected as the cathode with Na metal anode to assemble a coin cell. Rate performance of Na||NVP coupled with both electrolytes were evaluated. NVP paired with 0.5 M NaPF $_{6}$ G2/DOL achieves a capacity of up to 74.7 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 10 C, while it exclusively remains 60.6 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 10 C with 0.5 M NaPF $_{6}$ G2, as demonstrated in Figures S22–S24 (Supporting Information). Surprisingly, it can operate normally at LT, and specifically preserve a capacity of 79.8 mAh g $^{-1}$ at $-40$ °C, which is equivalent to 80.0% of the capacity at 25 °C in Figure S25 (Supporting Information). This indicates that temperature-adaptive electrolytes are not only compatible with NVP, but can also upgrade the rate performance and low-temperature performance of NVP cathode. To further verify the feasibility of electrolytes in SIBs, the coin full cell with NVP cathode and pre-cycled HC anode was assembled and subjected to rate performance testing at 25 °C. It displays that the full cell coupled with 0.5 M NaPF $_{6}$ G2/DOL can still retain a capacity of 71.6 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 10 C, while the cell using 0.5 M NaPF $_{6}$ G2 can only bestow a capacity of 52.3 mAh g $^{-1}$ in Figure 6a.

source_refs.raw_quote: Typically, this is on account of faster ion diffusion of 0.5 M NaPF $_{6}$ G2/DOL paired with HC, resulting in smaller voltage polarization at high current densities and low temperatures. This allows HC to achieve higher capacity at low temperatures and high rates. Additionally, the cycling performance of the HC anode at 25, -40, and $-50^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ was tested in Figure 5j and Figures S20, and S21 (Supporting Information). Compared with $78.9\%$ of $0.5\mathrm{MNaPF}_6$ G2, the capacity retention rate of HC after 1000 cycles at $5\mathrm{C}$ in $0.5\mathrm{MNaPF}_6$ G2/DOL is as high as $88.5\%$ at $25^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , indicating that HC has better stability with high current densities in $0.5\mathrm{MNaPF}_6$ G2/DOL. Besides, HC exhibits excellent low-temperature performance in $0.5\mathrm{MNaPF}_6$ G2/DOL. After 900 cycles at $-40^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , the capacity retention rate is $91.9\%$ . The capacity retention rates after 200 cycles at $1\mathrm{C}$ at $25^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and $-50^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ are $94.48\%$ and $97.25\%$ , respectively. This superior performance is attributed to the low-temperature adaptive solvation structure. Enhanced anion coordination and weakened solvent coordination facilitate to the desolvation of $\mathrm{Na^{+}}$ on the HC and the formation of rich-inorganic SEI, resulting in more desirable than the currently reported low-temperature electrolytes for SIBs, as listed in Table S7 (Supporting Information).

source_refs.raw_quote: In summary, we present a low-temperature adaptive electrolyte that is compatible with high $Na^{+}$ desolvation rates for SIBs by regulating solvation structure. Due to the weakened ion-dipole interaction of $Na^{+}-O$ (G2), 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2/DOL has a low-temperature responsive solvation structure. As the temperature decreases, solvent coordination reduces and anion coordination increases in the first solvated shell of $Na^{+}$ . The temperature-sensitive solvation structure accelerates the desolvation of $Na^{+}$ , mitigating the voltage polarization on the HC surface. This enables HC to achieve higher capacity retention at high current density and low temperatures, thereby enhancing the low-temperature performance of SIBs. The HC anode realized a high capacity of 220.8 mAh g $^{-1}$ (1 C) at -40 °C, with 91.9% capacity retention after 900 cycles. At -30 °C, the capacity retention rate of HC||NVP pouch cell after 100 cycles at 0.1 C is 92.43%, indicating that electrolytes with low-temperature adaptation can effectively improve the low-temperature performance of SIBs. Noteworthy, temperature-adapted solvation structures universally exist in G2/DOL derivative electrolytes, which have exceedingly outstanding low-temperature performance. This provides a new way for designing low-temperature sodium-ion batteries and broadens their application for energy storage in extremely cold regions.

source_refs.raw_quote:
Yuewei Cui, Youxuan Ni, Yuankun Wang, Linyue Wang, Wenxuan Yang, Shuang Wu, Weiwei Xie, Kai Zhang, Zhenhua Yan,\* and Jun Chen\*

Sodium-ion batteries are applied to cold-resistant energy storage hindered by phase transitions and sluggish $Na^{+}$ migration of traditional carbonate-based electrolytes at low temperatures. The desolvation of $Na^{+}$ is a crucial step in impeding the transport of $Na^{+}$ , which primarily attributes to the robust solvent coordination of $Na^{+}$ . Herein, a low-temperature adaptive electrolyte with an ultraweakly coordinated 1,3-dioxolane (DOL) is designed for constructing anion-rich solvation structure in a diglyme (G2)-based electrolyte. The electronegativity of the oxygen atoms of G2 is attenuated by dipole-dipole interaction between DOL and G2. As the temperature drops, the weakened $Na^{+}-O$ (G2) interaction leads to increased anionic coordination and less solvent coordination, facilitating the desolvation of $Na^{+}$ . This anionic-enhanced solvation structure contributes to the formation of stable solid electrolyte interface at the hard carbon (HC) anode, which accelerates $Na^{+}$ transport and diminishing the voltage polarization at low temperatures. Consequently, the HC anode can retain a high capacity of 203.9 mAh g $^{-1}$ (1 C) at -50 °C, and the pouch cell composed of $HC||Na_{3}V_{2}(PO_{4})_{3}$ at -30 °C achieves a capacity retention of 92.43% after 100 cycles at 0.1 C.

source_refs.raw_quote: Furthermore, the fluorination strategy relies on the controlled decomposition of fluorinated solvents or fluorine-rich additives to form a NaF-enriched inorganic interface, which significantly improves interfacial stability. $^{[24-26]}$ However, low-polarity solvents (e.g., cyclic ethers) used in weakly solvating strategies suffer from insufficient dissociation of sodium salts, resulting in limited ionic conductivity and flammability concerns due to their low flash points. Concentrated electrolytes and fluorination systems are also associated with high-cost concerns. Therefore, addressing the coupled challenges of temperature-resistant bulk/interface stability, cost-effectiveness, and safety remains a significant obstacle for large-scale energy storage applications. Herein, we design a flame-retardant hybrid electrolyte by combining fire-retardant triethyl phosphate (TEP) and low-freezing-point and weak-coordination methyl propionate (MP) solvents, which may offer the advantages of an anion-reinforced weak solvation structure, high nonflammability, and enhanced ionic conductivity at medium concentration (2 M). Fire-retardant TEP serves as the primary solvent to ensure salt solubility and nonflammability, while the introduction of MP, characterized by a lower freezing points and low dipole moment, aims to enhance ionic conductivity, reduce solvation energy, and facilitate the incorporation of additional anions into the Na $^{+}$ solvation structure.

source_refs.raw_quote: The Na+-MP complex exhibits a low binding energy (-1.38 eV), consistent with its low DN value, further validating the weak coordination ability of MP. The redox behavior of the electrolyte was further evaluated using molecular orbital theory (Figure S3, Supporting Information). PF6− possesses the lowest highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) energy level (-10.16 eV), indicating strong resistance to electron loss and enhanced oxidative stability. Moreover, its low lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO) suggests preferential decomposition at the negative electrode, thereby improving interfacial compatibility with TEP. Based on optimizations in nonflammability, ionic conductivity and long cycle performance, the 2.0 M NaPF6 in TEP/MP +1 wt% VC (6:4 by volume ratio, denoted as NTM) is selected as the optimal electrolyte for further investigation (Figures S2 and S4, Supporting Information), with 2.0 M NaPF6 dissolved in TEP +1 wt% VC (denoted as NT) and traditional carbonate electrolyte 1.0 M NaPF6 in PC (denoted as NP) serving as control groups. Moreover, the NTM electrolyte not only exhibits a reduced contact angle with the separator (Figure S5, Supporting Information), indicative of decreased electrolyte viscosity and improved wettability, but also shows an oxidation potential of up to 4.52 V and a lower reduction potential (Figure S6, Supporting Information).

2.4. Electrochemical Performance of Full Cell
We also have tested the low-temperature performance of 0.5 M NaPF $_{6}$ G2/DOL in the cathode material of SIBs. Na $_{3}$ V $_{2}$ (PO $_{4}$ ) $_{3}$ was selected as the cathode with Na metal anode to assemble a coin cell. Rate performance of Na||NVP coupled with both electrolytes were evaluated. NVP paired with 0.5 M NaPF $_{6}$ G2/DOL achieves a capacity of up to 74.7 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 10 C, while it exclusively remains 60.6 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 10 C with 0.5 M NaPF $_{6}$ G2, as demonstrated in Figures S22–S24 (Supporting Information). Surprisingly, it can operate normally at LT, and specifically preserve a capacity of 79.8 mAh g $^{-1}$ at $-40$ °C, which is equivalent to 80.0% of the capacity at 25 °C in Figure S25 (Supporting Information). This indicates that temperature-adaptive electrolytes are not only compatible with NVP, but can also upgrade the rate performance and low-temperature performance of NVP cathode.

To further verify the feasibility of electrolytes in SIBs, the coin full cell with NVP cathode and pre-cycled HC anode was assembled and subjected to rate performance testing at 25 °C. It displays that the full cell coupled with 0.5 M NaPF $_{6}$ G2/DOL can still retain a capacity of 71.6 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 10 C, while the cell using 0.5 M NaPF $_{6}$ G2 can only bestow a capacity of 52.3 mAh g $^{-1}$ in Figure 6a. Additionally, the performance of the full cell was evaluated at -40 °C and it was manifested that the full cell using 0.5 M NaPF $_{6}$ G2/DOL can preserve 64.8% of its capacity at 25 °C in Figure 6b. After 50 cycles of 0.1 C (10 mA g $^{-1}$ ) at 25 °C, the capacity retention rate was 95.7%, and then after 50 cycles of 0.1 C at -40 °C, the capacity retention rate was 92.8%, as shown in Figure 6c. To test the practical application of electrolytes, a piece pouch cell (45 mAh) was assembled for cycling testing in Figure 6d and Figure S26 (Supporting Information). After cycling 100 cycles at 25 °C, the capacity retention rate was 86.7%. Then, the pouch cell was cycled 100 cycles at -30 °C, and the capacity retention rate was 92.43% in Figure 6e. Therefore, 0.5 M NaPF $_{6}$ G2/DOL electrolyte with a temperature-adaptive solvent structure holds great potential in the practical application of SIBs.

citations.chunk_id: 0009_Cui 等 - 2025 - A Temperature-Adapted Ultraweakly Solvating Electrolyte for Cold-Resistant Sodium-Ion Batteries::sec2::child0
citations.quote: Primarily, $Na^{+}-O$ (DOL) has a lower binding energy compared to $Na^{+}-O$ (G2), as shown in Figure 2a. Additionally, $Na^{+}$ can form a stable five-membered chelation structure with the negative-charged multidentate oxygen of G2 molecules. This endows the G2-based electrolyte high ionic conductivity, but regretfully, impedes $Na^{+}$ desolvation. DOL is a low polarity and low melting point ( $-95\ ^{\circ}C$ ) cyclic ether that exhibits dipole-dipole interactions with G2. Explicitly, ${}^{1}H$ and ${}^{17}O$ nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) were studied in Figure 2b; Figure S1 (Supporting Information). ${}^{1}H$ (G2) displays an upfield chemical shift in G2/DOL than G2, while the chemical shift of the ${}^{17}O$ (G2) shifts downfield. This implies that the dipole-dipole interactions between G2 and DOL weaken the shielding effect of electron clouds of O (G2) on atomic nucleus, indicating a decrease in the electron cloud density of O (G2). This demonstrates that DOL attenuates the electronegativity of donor O (G2), thereby diminishing the coordination of G2. $^{[16]}$ Consequently, DOL was blended into 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2 with a volume ratio of 3:1 to prepare 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2/DOL for the low-temperature adaptive electrolyte. 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2 as the reference electrolyte was compared and analyzed.

citations.chunk_id: 0009_Cui 等 - 2025 - A Temperature-Adapted Ultraweakly Solvating Electrolyte for Cold-Resistant Sodium-Ion Batteries::sec6::child0
citations.quote: In summary, we present a low-temperature adaptive electrolyte that is compatible with high $Na^{+}$ desolvation rates for SIBs by regulating solvation structure. Due to the weakened ion-dipole interaction of $Na^{+}-O$ (G2), 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2/DOL has a low-temperature responsive solvation structure. As the temperature decreases, solvent coordination reduces and anion coordination increases in the first solvated shell of $Na^{+}$ . The temperature-sensitive solvation structure accelerates the desolvation of $Na^{+}$ , mitigating the voltage polarization on the HC surface. This enables HC to achieve higher capacity retention at high current density and low temperatures, thereby enhancing the low-temperature performance of SIBs. The HC anode realized a high capacity of 220.8 mAh g $^{-1}$ (1 C) at -40 °C, with 91.9% capacity retention after 900 cycles. At -30 °C, the capacity retention rate of HC||NVP pouch cell after 100 cycles at 0.1 C is 92.43%, indicating that electrolytes with low-temperature adaptation can effectively improve the low-temperature performance of SIBs. Noteworthy, temperature-adapted solvation structures universally exist in G2/DOL derivative electrolytes, which have exceedingly outstanding low-temperature performance. This provides a new way for designing low-temperature sodium-ion batteries and broadens their application for energy storage in extremely cold regions.

After 50 cycles of 0.1 C (10 mA g $^{-1}$ ) at 25 °C, the capacity retention rate was 95.7%, and then after 50 cycles of 0.1 C at -40 °C, the capacity retention rate was 92.8%, as shown in Figure 6c. We also have tested the low-temperature performance of 0.5 M NaPF $_{6}$ G2/DOL in the cathode material of SIBs. Na $_{3}$ V $_{2}$ (PO $_{4}$ ) $_{3}$ was selected as the cathode with Na metal anode to assemble a coin cell. Rate performance of Na||NVP coupled with both electrolytes were evaluated. NVP paired with 0.5 M NaPF $_{6}$ G2/DOL achieves a capacity of up to 74.7 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 10 C, while it exclusively remains 60.6 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 10 C with 0.5 M NaPF $_{6}$ G2, as demonstrated in Figures S22–S24 (Supporting Information). Surprisingly, it can operate normally at LT, and specifically preserve a capacity of 79.8 mAh g $^{-1}$ at $-40$ °C, which is equivalent to 80.0% of the capacity at 25 °C in Figure S25 (Supporting Information). This indicates that temperature-adaptive electrolytes are not only compatible with NVP, but can also upgrade the rate performance and low-temperature performance of NVP cathode.

To further verify the feasibility of electrolytes in SIBs, the coin full cell with NVP cathode and pre-cycled HC anode was assembled and subjected to rate performance testing at 25 °C. citations.quote: The Na+-MP complex exhibits a low binding energy (-1.38 eV), consistent with its low DN value, further validating the weak coordination ability of MP. The redox behavior of the electrolyte was further evaluated using molecular orbital theory (Figure S3, Supporting Information). PF6− possesses the lowest highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) energy level (-10.16 eV), indicating strong resistance to electron loss and enhanced oxidative stability. Moreover, its low lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO) suggests preferential decomposition at the negative electrode, thereby improving interfacial compatibility with TEP. Based on optimizations in nonflammability, ionic conductivity and long cycle performance, the 2.0 M NaPF6 in TEP/MP +1 wt% VC (6:4 by volume ratio, denoted as NTM) is selected as the optimal electrolyte for further investigation (Figures S2 and S4, Supporting Information), with 2.0 M NaPF6 dissolved in TEP +1 wt% VC (denoted as NT) and traditional carbonate electrolyte 1.0 M NaPF6 in PC (denoted as NP) serving as control groups. Moreover, the NTM electrolyte not only exhibits a reduced contact angle with the separator (Figure S5, Supporting Information), indicative of decreased electrolyte viscosity and improved wettability, but also shows an oxidation potential of up to 4.52 V and a lower reduction potential (Figure S6, Supporting Information).

This endows the G2-based electrolyte high ionic conductivity, but regretfully, impedes $Na^{+}$ desolvation. DOL is a low polarity and low melting point ( $-95\ ^{\circ}C$ ) cyclic ether that exhibits dipole-dipole interactions with G2. Explicitly, ${}^{1}H$ and ${}^{17}O$ nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) were studied in Figure 2b; Figure S1 (Supporting Information). ${}^{1}H$ (G2) displays an upfield chemical shift in G2/DOL than G2, while the chemical shift of the ${}^{17}O$ (G2) shifts downfield. This implies that the dipole-dipole interactions between G2 and DOL weaken the shielding effect of electron clouds of O (G2) on atomic nucleus, indicating a decrease in the electron cloud density of O (G2). This demonstrates that DOL attenuates the electronegativity of donor O (G2), thereby diminishing the coordination of G2. $^{[16]}$ Consequently, DOL was blended into 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2 with a volume ratio of 3:1 to prepare 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2/DOL for the low-temperature adaptive electrolyte. 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2 as the reference electrolyte was compared and analyzed.

Compared with $78.9\%$ of $0.5\mathrm{MNaPF}_6$ G2, the capacity retention rate of HC after 1000 cycles at $5\mathrm{C}$ in $0.5\mathrm{MNaPF}_6$ G2/DOL is as high as $88.5\%$ at $25^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , indicating that HC has better stability with high current densities in $0.5\mathrm{MNaPF}_6$ G2/DOL. Besides, HC exhibits excellent low-temperature performance in $0.5\mathrm{MNaPF}_6$ G2/DOL. After 900 cycles at $-40^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , the capacity retention rate is $91.9\%$ . The capacity retention rates after 200 cycles at $1\mathrm{C}$ at $25^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and $-50^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ are $94.48\%$ and $97.25\%$ , respectively. This superior performance is attributed to the low-temperature adaptive solvation structure. Enhanced anion coordination and weakened solvent coordination facilitate to the desolvation of $\mathrm{Na^{+}}$ on the HC and the formation of rich-inorganic SEI, resulting in more desirable than the currently reported low-temperature electrolytes for SIBs, as listed in Table S7 (Supporting Information).

evidence_ledger.paper_id: 0009_Cui 等 - 2025 - A Temperature-Adapted Ultraweakly Solvating Electrolyte for Cold-Resistant Sodium-Ion Batteries
evidence_ledger.quote: In summary, we present a low-temperature adaptive electrolyte that is compatible with high $Na^{+}$ desolvation rates for SIBs by regulating solvation structure. Due to the weakened ion-dipole interaction of $Na^{+}-O$ (G2), 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2/DOL has a low-temperature responsive solvation structure. As the temperature decreases, solvent coordination reduces and anion coordination increases in the first solvated shell of $Na^{+}$ . The temperature-sensitive solvation structure accelerates the desolvation of $Na^{+}$ , mitigating the voltage polarization on the HC surface. This enables HC to achieve higher capacity retention at high current density and low temperatures, thereby enhancing the low-temperature performance of SIBs. The HC anode realized a high capacity of 220.8 mAh g $^{-1}$ (1 C) at -40 °C, with 91.9% capacity retention after 900 cycles. At -30 °C, the capacity retention rate of HC||NVP pouch cell after 100 cycles at 0.1 C is 92.43%, indicating that electrolytes with low-temperature adaptation can effectively improve the low-temperature performance of SIBs. Noteworthy, temperature-adapted solvation structures universally exist in G2/DOL derivative electrolytes, which have exceedingly outstanding low-temperature performance. This provides a new way for designing low-temperature sodium-ion batteries and broadens their application for energy storage in extremely cold regions.

evidence_ledger.chunk_id: 0009_Cui 等 - 2025 - A Temperature-Adapted Ultraweakly Solvating Electrolyte for Cold-Resistant Sodium-Ion Batteries::sec0::child0
evidence_ledger.paper_id: 0009_Cui 等 - 2025 - A Temperature-Adapted Ultraweakly Solvating Electrolyte for Cold-Resistant Sodium-Ion Batteries
evidence_ledger.quote:
Yuewei Cui, Youxuan Ni, Yuankun Wang, Linyue Wang, Wenxuan Yang, Shuang Wu, Weiwei Xie, Kai Zhang, Zhenhua Yan,\* and Jun Chen\*

Sodium-ion batteries are applied to cold-resistant energy storage hindered by phase transitions and sluggish $Na^{+}$ migration of traditional carbonate-based electrolytes at low temperatures. The desolvation of $Na^{+}$ is a crucial step in impeding the transport of $Na^{+}$ , which primarily attributes to the robust solvent coordination of $Na^{+}$ . Herein, a low-temperature adaptive electrolyte with an ultraweakly coordinated 1,3-dioxolane (DOL) is designed for constructing anion-rich solvation structure in a diglyme (G2)-based electrolyte. The electronegativity of the oxygen atoms of G2 is attenuated by dipole-dipole interaction between DOL and G2. As the temperature drops, the weakened $Na^{+}-O$ (G2) interaction leads to increased anionic coordination and less solvent coordination, facilitating the desolvation of $Na^{+}$ . This anionic-enhanced solvation structure contributes to the formation of stable solid electrolyte interface at the hard carbon (HC) anode, which accelerates $Na^{+}$ transport and diminishing the voltage polarization at low temperatures. Consequently, the HC anode can retain a high capacity of 203.9 mAh g $^{-1}$ (1 C) at -50 °C, and the pouch cell composed of $HC||Na_{3}V_{2}(PO_{4})_{3}$ at -30 °C achieves a capacity retention of 92.43% after 100 cycles at 0.1 C.

evidence_ledger.quote: Furthermore, the fluorination strategy relies on the controlled decomposition of fluorinated solvents or fluorine-rich additives to form a NaF-enriched inorganic interface, which significantly improves interfacial stability. $^{[24-26]}$ However, low-polarity solvents (e.g., cyclic ethers) used in weakly solvating strategies suffer from insufficient dissociation of sodium salts, resulting in limited ionic conductivity and flammability concerns due to their low flash points. Concentrated electrolytes and fluorination systems are also associated with high-cost concerns. Therefore, addressing the coupled challenges of temperature-resistant bulk/interface stability, cost-effectiveness, and safety remains a significant obstacle for large-scale energy storage applications. Herein, we design a flame-retardant hybrid electrolyte by combining fire-retardant triethyl phosphate (TEP) and low-freezing-point and weak-coordination methyl propionate (MP) solvents, which may offer the advantages of an anion-reinforced weak solvation structure, high nonflammability, and enhanced ionic conductivity at medium concentration (2 M). Fire-retardant TEP serves as the primary solvent to ensure salt solubility and nonflammability, while the introduction of MP, characterized by a lower freezing points and low dipole moment, aims to enhance ionic conductivity, reduce solvation energy, and facilitate the incorporation of additional anions into the Na $^{+}$ solvation structure.

2.4. Electrochemical Performance of Full Cell
We also have tested the low-temperature performance of 0.5 M NaPF $_{6}$ G2/DOL in the cathode material of SIBs. Na $_{3}$ V $_{2}$ (PO $_{4}$ ) $_{3}$ was selected as the cathode with Na metal anode to assemble a coin cell. Rate performance of Na||NVP coupled with both electrolytes were evaluated. NVP paired with 0.5 M NaPF $_{6}$ G2/DOL achieves a capacity of up to 74.7 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 10 C, while it exclusively remains 60.6 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 10 C with 0.5 M NaPF $_{6}$ G2, as demonstrated in Figures S22–S24 (Supporting Information). Surprisingly, it can operate normally at LT, and specifically preserve a capacity of 79.8 mAh g $^{-1}$ at $-40$ °C, which is equivalent to 80.0% of the capacity at 25 °C in Figure S25 (Supporting Information). This indicates that temperature-adaptive electrolytes are not only compatible with NVP, but can also upgrade the rate performance and low-temperature performance of NVP cathode.

This endows the G2-based electrolyte high ionic conductivity, but regretfully, impedes $Na^{+}$ desolvation. DOL is a low polarity and low melting point ( $-95\ ^{\circ}C$ ) cyclic ether that exhibits dipole-dipole interactions with G2. Explicitly, ${}^{1}H$ and ${}^{17}O$ nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) were studied in Figure 2b; Figure S1 (Supporting Information). ${}^{1}H$ (G2) displays an upfield chemical shift in G2/DOL than G2, while the chemical shift of the ${}^{17}O$ (G2) shifts downfield. This implies that the dipole-dipole interactions between G2 and DOL weaken the shielding effect of electron clouds of O (G2) on atomic nucleus, indicating a decrease in the electron cloud density of O (G2). This demonstrates that DOL attenuates the electronegativity of donor O (G2), thereby diminishing the coordination of G2. $^{[16]}$ Consequently, DOL was blended into 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2 with a volume ratio of 3:1 to prepare 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2/DOL for the low-temperature adaptive electrolyte. 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2 as the reference electrolyte was compared and analyzed.

citations.chunk_id: 0009_Cui 等 - 2025 - A Temperature-Adapted Ultraweakly Solvating Electrolyte for Cold-Resistant Sodium-Ion Batteries::sec6::child0
citations.quote: In summary, we present a low-temperature adaptive electrolyte that is compatible with high $Na^{+}$ desolvation rates for SIBs by regulating solvation structure. Due to the weakened ion-dipole interaction of $Na^{+}-O$ (G2), 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2/DOL has a low-temperature responsive solvation structure. As the temperature decreases, solvent coordination reduces and anion coordination increases in the first solvated shell of $Na^{+}$ . The temperature-sensitive solvation structure accelerates the desolvation of $Na^{+}$ , mitigating the voltage polarization on the HC surface. This enables HC to achieve higher capacity retention at high current density and low temperatures, thereby enhancing the low-temperature performance of SIBs. The HC anode realized a high capacity of 220.8 mAh g $^{-1}$ (1 C) at -40 °C, with 91.9% capacity retention after 900 cycles. At -30 °C, the capacity retention rate of HC||NVP pouch cell after 100 cycles at 0.1 C is 92.43%, indicating that electrolytes with low-temperature adaptation can effectively improve the low-temperature performance of SIBs. Noteworthy, temperature-adapted solvation structures universally exist in G2/DOL derivative electrolytes, which have exceedingly outstanding low-temperature performance. This provides a new way for designing low-temperature sodium-ion batteries and broadens their application for energy storage in extremely cold regions.

citations.quote: Materials: $NaPF_{6}$ was purchased from Dodochem. Tetrahydrofuran (THF), 2-methyltetrahydrofuran (MTHF), 3-methyltetrahydrofuran (3-MTHF), 1,3-dioxane (DOL), 2-methyl-1,3-dioxolane (2-MDOL), 4-methyl-1,3-dioxolane (4-MDOL), tetrahydropyran (THP), 1,3-dioxane (1,3-DX) and 1,4-dioxane (1,4-DX) were ordered from Aladdin. The electrolytes were obtained by dissolving 1 M $NaPF_{6}$ in THF/cyclic ethers with different volume ratios. All the electrolytes were kept overnight prior to use to ensure complete dissolution. Preparation of Electrodes: To prepare the anodes, commercial $\mu$ -Sn powders ( $\geq99.5\%$ , 325 mesh, Alab Chem. Tech.), polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF, Dodochem), and acetylene black (AB, Dodochem) were uniformly mixed in a steel jar with a mass ratio of $\mu$ -Sn: AB: PVDF at 7:2:1. A suitable amount of N-methyl-2-pyrrolidone (NMP, 99.0%, Aladdin) was added dropwise into the jar to create a sticky slurry, which was then ball milled at 300 rpm for 4 h. The obtained slurry was evenly coated onto copper foil using a doctor blade and was dried overnight in a vacuum oven at 60 °C. The dried copper foil was punched into circular discs with a diameter of 10 mm, and the mass loading of $\mu$ -Sn was $\approx1.0-1.4$ mg cm $^{-2}$ . To prepare the cathodes, Na $_{3}$ V $_{2}$ (PO $_{4}$ ) $_{3}$ @C (NVP@C) was synthesized by a reported method. NVP@C, AB, and PVDF were uniformly mixed with a weight ratio of 8:1:1.

citations.quote: First of all, different ratios of THF and MTHF in the electrolyte are tested at -40 °C. As illustrated in Figure S3 (Supporting Information), the half cells using the electrolyte with a volume ratio of THF/MTHF (TMT) at 3:7 v v $^{-1}$ show the highest reversible capacity, surpassing the performance of THF, MTHF, and THF/MTHF at other ratios. Thus, the following discussion focuses on this electrolyte, denoted as N/TMT. Meanwhile, the other two electrolytes, NaPF $_{6}$ dissolved in THF (N/THF) or MTHF (N/MTHF), were used as references. Then, MD simulations are employed to unveil the solvation structures in N/THF, N/TMT, and N/MTHF at $-40\ ^{\circ}C$ . As shown in Figure 1a–c, all three electrolytes contain abundant CIP (contact-ion pair) and AGG (Aggregates) structures, where anions are incorporated in the solvation sheath together with solvent molecules. This feature facilitates the formation of inorganic-rich SEI exhibiting superior mechanical properties. Therefore, these structures are highly desirable for high-stability anode materials. $^{[13]}$ The careful examination of these structures reveals that the coordination numbers (CNs) of $Na^{+}-F$ in N/THF, N/TMT, and N/MTHF increase from 2.44, 2.92 to 3.08 (Figure 1d–f), attributing to the low dielectric constant and weak binding ability of MTHF. While those of $Na^{+}-O$ in N/THF, N/TMT, and N/MTHF decrease from 3.67, 2.59 to 2.24 as a consequence of the increasing anions in the solvation sheath.

Tetrahydrofuran (THF), 2-methyltetrahydrofuran (MTHF), 3-methyltetrahydrofuran (3-MTHF), 1,3-dioxane (DOL), 2-methyl-1,3-dioxolane (2-MDOL), 4-methyl-1,3-dioxolane (4-MDOL), tetrahydropyran (THP), 1,3-dioxane (1,3-DX) and 1,4-dioxane (1,4-DX) were ordered from Aladdin. The electrolytes were obtained by dissolving 1 M $NaPF_{6}$ in THF/cyclic ethers with different volume ratios. All the electrolytes were kept overnight prior to use to ensure complete dissolution. Preparation of Electrodes: To prepare the anodes, commercial $\mu$ -Sn powders ( $\geq99.5\%$ , 325 mesh, Alab Chem. Tech.), polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF, Dodochem), and acetylene black (AB, Dodochem) were uniformly mixed in a steel jar with a mass ratio of $\mu$ -Sn: AB: PVDF at 7:2:1. A suitable amount of N-methyl-2-pyrrolidone (NMP, 99.0%, Aladdin) was added dropwise into the jar to create a sticky slurry, which was then ball milled at 300 rpm for 4 h. The obtained slurry was evenly coated onto copper foil using a doctor blade and was dried overnight in a vacuum oven at 60 °C. The dried copper foil was punched into circular discs with a diameter of 10 mm, and the mass loading of $\mu$ -Sn was $\approx1.0-1.4$ mg cm $^{-2}$ . To prepare the cathodes, Na $_{3}$ V $_{2}$ (PO $_{4}$ ) $_{3}$ @C (NVP@C) was synthesized by a reported method. NVP@C, AB, and PVDF were uniformly mixed with a weight ratio of 8:1:1.

citations.quote: The Na+-MP complex exhibits a low binding energy (-1.38 eV), consistent with its low DN value, further validating the weak coordination ability of MP. The redox behavior of the electrolyte was further evaluated using molecular orbital theory (Figure S3, Supporting Information). PF6− possesses the lowest highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) energy level (-10.16 eV), indicating strong resistance to electron loss and enhanced oxidative stability. Moreover, its low lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO) suggests preferential decomposition at the negative electrode, thereby improving interfacial compatibility with TEP. Based on optimizations in nonflammability, ionic conductivity and long cycle performance, the 2.0 M NaPF6 in TEP/MP +1 wt% VC (6:4 by volume ratio, denoted as NTM) is selected as the optimal electrolyte for further investigation (Figures S2 and S4, Supporting Information), with 2.0 M NaPF6 dissolved in TEP +1 wt% VC (denoted as NT) and traditional carbonate electrolyte 1.0 M NaPF6 in PC (denoted as NP) serving as control groups. Moreover, the NTM electrolyte not only exhibits a reduced contact angle with the separator (Figure S5, Supporting Information), indicative of decreased electrolyte viscosity and improved wettability, but also shows an oxidation potential of up to 4.52 V and a lower reduction potential (Figure S6, Supporting Information).

citations.quote: To further validate the practicality of the NTM electrolyte, full cells with NVP cathodes and hard carbon (HC) anodes were constructed, operating within the voltage range of 2.0–3.6 V (Figure 5a). The NVP||HC full cell, without any presodiation treatment, exhibits a high specific capacity of 88.0 mA h g $^{-1}$ and excellent cycling stability over 100 cycles at 50 mA g $^{-1}$ , maintaining an impressive capacity retention of 84.9% in the NTM electrolyte. This retention markedly surpasses that of the conventional NP electrolyte (51.9%), as illustrated in Figure 5b,c. Furthermore, the full cell utilizing the NTM electrolyte demonstrates superior rate capability, delivering reversible capacities of 87.2, 82.0, 79.1, 77.0, 71.9, and 68.1 mA h g $^{-1}$ at 20, 50, 80, 100, 200, and 300 mA g $^{-1}$ , respectively (Figure 5d). The charge–discharge curves exhibit minimal polarization even at elevated rates (Figure S32, Supporting Information). In addition, the overall electrical performance of the NTM electrolyte is better than that of the NED (NP-EC/DMC) electrolyte (Figure S33, Supporting Information). Notably, the NVP||HC full cell with the NTM electrolyte maintains stable cycling for 500 cycles at a high current of 200 mA g $^{-1}$ (Figure S34, Supporting Information). Self-discharge behavior was further evaluated in the NVP||HC full-cell system. The results display that the NP electrolyte system retains 72.8% of its discharge capacity after 48 h of rest (based on 4th cycle).

citations.chunk_id: 0009_Cui 等 - 2025 - A Temperature-Adapted Ultraweakly Solvating Electrolyte for Cold-Resistant Sodium-Ion Batteries::sec2::child0
citations.quote: Primarily, $Na^{+}-O$ (DOL) has a lower binding energy compared to $Na^{+}-O$ (G2), as shown in Figure 2a. Additionally, $Na^{+}$ can form a stable five-membered chelation structure with the negative-charged multidentate oxygen of G2 molecules. This endows the G2-based electrolyte high ionic conductivity, but regretfully, impedes $Na^{+}$ desolvation. DOL is a low polarity and low melting point ( $-95\ ^{\circ}C$ ) cyclic ether that exhibits dipole-dipole interactions with G2. Explicitly, ${}^{1}H$ and ${}^{17}O$ nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) were studied in Figure 2b; Figure S1 (Supporting Information). ${}^{1}H$ (G2) displays an upfield chemical shift in G2/DOL than G2, while the chemical shift of the ${}^{17}O$ (G2) shifts downfield. This implies that the dipole-dipole interactions between G2 and DOL weaken the shielding effect of electron clouds of O (G2) on atomic nucleus, indicating a decrease in the electron cloud density of O (G2). This demonstrates that DOL attenuates the electronegativity of donor O (G2), thereby diminishing the coordination of G2. $^{[16]}$ Consequently, DOL was blended into 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2 with a volume ratio of 3:1 to prepare 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2/DOL for the low-temperature adaptive electrolyte. 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2 as the reference electrolyte was compared and analyzed.

citations.chunk_id: 0009_Cui 等 - 2025 - A Temperature-Adapted Ultraweakly Solvating Electrolyte for Cold-Resistant Sodium-Ion Batteries::sec6::child0
citations.quote: In summary, we present a low-temperature adaptive electrolyte that is compatible with high $Na^{+}$ desolvation rates for SIBs by regulating solvation structure. Due to the weakened ion-dipole interaction of $Na^{+}-O$ (G2), 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2/DOL has a low-temperature responsive solvation structure. As the temperature decreases, solvent coordination reduces and anion coordination increases in the first solvated shell of $Na^{+}$ . The temperature-sensitive solvation structure accelerates the desolvation of $Na^{+}$ , mitigating the voltage polarization on the HC surface. This enables HC to achieve higher capacity retention at high current density and low temperatures, thereby enhancing the low-temperature performance of SIBs. The HC anode realized a high capacity of 220.8 mAh g $^{-1}$ (1 C) at -40 °C, with 91.9% capacity retention after 900 cycles. At -30 °C, the capacity retention rate of HC||NVP pouch cell after 100 cycles at 0.1 C is 92.43%, indicating that electrolytes with low-temperature adaptation can effectively improve the low-temperature performance of SIBs. Noteworthy, temperature-adapted solvation structures universally exist in G2/DOL derivative electrolytes, which have exceedingly outstanding low-temperature performance. This provides a new way for designing low-temperature sodium-ion batteries and broadens their application for energy storage in extremely cold regions.

Additionally, $Na^{+}$ can form a stable five-membered chelation structure with the negative-charged multidentate oxygen of G2 molecules. This endows the G2-based electrolyte high ionic conductivity, but regretfully, impedes $Na^{+}$ desolvation. DOL is a low polarity and low melting point ( $-95\ ^{\circ}C$ ) cyclic ether that exhibits dipole-dipole interactions with G2. Explicitly, ${}^{1}H$ and ${}^{17}O$ nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) were studied in Figure 2b; Figure S1 (Supporting Information). ${}^{1}H$ (G2) displays an upfield chemical shift in G2/DOL than G2, while the chemical shift of the ${}^{17}O$ (G2) shifts downfield. This implies that the dipole-dipole interactions between G2 and DOL weaken the shielding effect of electron clouds of O (G2) on atomic nucleus, indicating a decrease in the electron cloud density of O (G2). This demonstrates that DOL attenuates the electronegativity of donor O (G2), thereby diminishing the coordination of G2. $^{[16]}$ Consequently, DOL was blended into 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2 with a volume ratio of 3:1 to prepare 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2/DOL for the low-temperature adaptive electrolyte. 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2 as the reference electrolyte was compared and analyzed.
